name: Phrase counting
lesson:
## Count in phrases, not bars

House and techno move in 8-bar phrases; most changes (drops, breakdowns, new elements) land on a 16- or 32-bar boundary. Tap hot cue A1 on the first beat of every 8-bar phrase for 64 bars. Prompts are shown, but the aim is to hit them from your own count with the prompt only confirming you.

Every other drill assumes you can feel these boundaries without looking. If your timing here is over 60 ms, stay on this one.

tracks.cue: The Monster Mix has one of the longest DJ intros in the canon. Start on the first kick and count 8-bar phrases; the vocal, the breakdown and the riff all arrive on 16- or 32-bar lines, so every one of your A1 presses should land where something changes.
Nine minutes of one slow crescendo. Elements are added on phrase boundaries, never mid-phrase, so if your count drifts you hear it immediately. Practise from the first kick through the peak.
Elements come in and out in 16-bar blocks over a bassline that never stops. Count from the first kick; when the vocoder hook arrives you should be on a phrase downbeat.
